findings.title: Login cache does not account for organization invalidation or dynamic enabled state
findings.body: getForLogin decides whether to use the cache only by checking isInvalid(cacheKey). It does not check whether the requested organization is invalidated (unlike getByOrganization, which checks isInvalid(orgId)), and the PR does not invalidate these login cache keys when an organization is removed or disabled. Because the organization-aware wrapper's isEnabled() can become false solely due to organization state, and getForLogin returns the resolved models without a final isEnabled() filter, stale cached entries can return providers that are no longer usable for login.

findings.title: Update invalidation can miss BROKER_PUBLIC changes for realm-level providers
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when both old and new models satisfy getLoginPredicate() and the organization ID is unchanged. For providers with organizationId == null, the predicate ignores BROKER_PUBLIC, but the default getForLogin for ORG_ONLY/ALL without a specific organization filters on BROKER_PUBLIC. Toggling that flag on a realm-level provider can therefore change the result set while the login cache remains valid.

findings.title: ORG_ONLY no-organization path may include realm-level providers with BROKER_PUBLIC
findings.body: The onlyOrganizationBrokers branch without a resolved organization calls getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, null) and filters only on isEnabled() and alias. The default getForLogin for ORG_ONLY without an organization adds BROKER_PUBLIC=true but does not require organizationId to be non-null, so a realm-level identity provider with BROKER_PUBLIC=true can be returned and displayed as an organization broker, contrary to the ORG_ONLY contract.

findings.title: Login cache entry can accumulate unbounded organization search keys
findings.body: getForLogin stores results for each distinct organizationId as a separate search key inside a single IdentityProviderListQuery keyed only by realm and FetchMode. In realms with many organizations, this cache entry can grow without bound as different organizations are resolved during login, increasing memory usage and making each invalidation discard all organization-specific login results.

findings.title: Test cleanup registers removal of literal 'alias' instead of the created aliases
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, cleanup is registered with testRealm().identityProviders().get('alias')::remove instead of using the created alias (for example 'idp-alias-' + i, and similarly at line 425 for 'idp-alias-20'). As a result, the created identity providers are not removed by this cleanup, and the cleanup may attempt to remove a non-existent provider named alias.
